items.title: Barcola: People are starting to understand me better - but I'm not Mo Salah
items.excerpt: Big money signings can take time to get going at their new club. There are plenty at Liverpool who can testify to that.
body: Big money signings can take time to get going at their new club. There are plenty at Liverpool who can testify to that.

As Sky Sports settles into a room at Liverpool's AXA training facility, a large window shows some of their big-money stars walking off one of the pitches after a recovery session. It's a sheer amount of attacking wealth.

Two of them are Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who arrived in deals that could reach a combined £241m. But the jury is still out on both of them. Isak has only just started delivering his highly-anticipated goal numbers, while many believe Wirtz is yet to get going on Merseyside.

This year, Bradley Barcola - who goes from the pitch to sitting in front of the Sky Sports cameras in the training facility - is the latest marquee signing, this time for £123m. But a slow start to life at Anfield brought about familiar concerns about recent buys. items.title: Could former wonderkid Silva fulfil his potential at Dortmund?
items.excerpt: While the Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was fluffing his lines at one end of the pitch, Fabio Silva was preparing to rewrite the script at the other. His late equaliser for Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker must be the most important goal…
body: While the Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was fluffing his lines at one end of the pitch, Fabio Silva was preparing to rewrite the script at the other. His late equaliser for Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker must be the most important goal of his career.

It was magnificent too. The first touch was perfection to protect the ball and give him just enough space to arrow a shot into the far corner with his second. An 89th-minute equaliser away to Bayern Munich to maintain Dortmund's unbeaten record.

There is a feeling within Dortmund that he needed this as a reward for his efforts. Speaking to goalkeeper Gregor Kobel afterwards, he made the point that forwards need goals to feel good. Stealing the show from Kane could be a transformative moment.

Silva's potential has long been debated. He was just 18 when Wolves committed £30m to sign him from Porto, the club's chairman talking of a generational talent.
